section_summaries.individual_presentation: progressive stiffness and pain in the lower back with intermittent cramps over a 3-year period; cramps were extremely painful; sensitivity to any sudden movement or external stimulation; lower back stiffness causing great difficulty performing daily activities and walking with a rigid and straight back; stiffness of the muscles subsided during normal sleep; left L5 radiculopathy progressive stiffness and pain in the lower back of 3 years' duration rigidity and pain in the lower back persisted and even progressed to the upper back and neck; limbs gradually affected with more severe symptoms proximally located; intermittent cramps easily induced by sudden movements or unexpected noise; walked slowly with a stiff spine and limbs; inability to bend waist; great difficulty performing daily activities, particularly putting on shoes and trousers; unable to drive a car due to limited neck mobility; muscular stiffness and pain subsided during normal sleep; speech was normal
section_summaries.individual_diagnostics: Electromyography showed spontaneous continuous muscle fiber activity which was markedly suppressed after a trial with 20 mg intravenous diazepam electromyograms showed continuous muscle fiber activity that responded dramatically to diazepam and fulfilled the diagnosis of SMS myelography and computed tomography of the whole spine showed a laterally protruding disc in the L5-S1 intervertebral space with compression of the left S1 root
section_summaries.individual_treatment: treatment with oral diazepam 80 mg daily, tapered to 15 mg daily received discectomy with subsequent medical and rehabilitation treatment; previous drug treatment included indomethacin, mefenamic acid, tolmetin, acetaminophen, baclofen, and fludiazepam oral diazepam therapy (initial dose 15 mg/day; maintenance dose 80 mg/day for 6 months); dosage tapered to 15 mg daily in the following 20-month period
section_summaries.individual_outcome: muscular stiffness disappeared during treatment with oral diazepam without any recurrence of spasm for 20 months muscular stiffness and cramps disappeared within one month; no drowsiness, weakness or respiratory suppression during diazepam therapy; patient was well and went back to work 6 months later; stiffness and pain did not recur The therapeutic response to diazepam ... is so effective and characteristic
section_summaries.individual_limitations: No history of trauma or infection was noted, and no family members had neurologic disorders No symptoms, signs, treatment, or outcome details were provided in the text
